# The Line to Kesslerpass

## I. The Valley

The train was already late when Elise Varga stepped onto the platform at Thalheim, her suitcase dragging a groan against the flagstones. She had expected precision. Everything about the Kesslerbahn was meant to be precise: the interlocking of steel teeth, the measured pitch of the rack, the punctuality of a system built by men who understood that a single miscalculation in gradient could send a car of passengers sliding backward into the valley like a stone off a finger. But the line from Unterthal had been closed that morning by a fallen birch, and the connecting service from the southern branch would not arrive until the last light bled from the eastern ridge.
